description: A six-note chord quantizer whose notes can be shuffled between the six outputs: a root and a chord type give six pitches, and each trigger applies a permutation that moves them from jack to jack

params.text: Picks which permutation is applied on each trigger
Attenuverts the weave CV before it is added to the weave knob
Picks the chord built on the root, from an octave through the major and minor triads to the ninths and suspensions printed round the knob
Drops the chord an octave on each press, as far as one octave down
Lifts the chord an octave on each press, as far as one octave up
Applies the chosen permutation on each press, moving every note to a different output
Returns the notes to their starting outputs on each press
Shifts every output, -1V to 1V, which the menu can snap to semitones

inputs.text: A rise applies the chosen permutation, moving every note to a different output
A rise returns the notes to their starting outputs
Picks the permutation, one volt per pattern, added to the weave knob and wrapped round the list
Sets the root of the chord as a volt per octave; a polyphonic cable here gives the six notes directly instead of building a chord
Picks the chord type, one twelfth of a volt per step through the list, wrapping round the sixteen chords
Shifts every output, added to the transpose knob; the menu can snap the total to semitones

outputs.text: Fires a one-millisecond 10V trigger whenever the notes change, from a weave, a chord change, a root change or an octave button
Carries all six notes at once as six polyphonic channels, each note on the channel its permutation has moved it to
One of the six chord notes as a volt per octave, clamped to -10 to 10V; which note arrives here depends on the permutation
The root of the chord as a volt per octave, put in the octave of the lowest note being played

notes: the chord is built from a root and a chord type, and the root comes from the keyboard drawn on the panel, from the ROOT NOTE input, or from both
the keyboard on the panel is a display rather than a control, so clicking one of its keys cannot reach a help entry
patching a polyphonic cable into the root input replaces the chord builder: the cable's channels become the notes, and the chord knob is ignored
menu: Quantize Shift to semitones — snaps the transpose knob and its CV to whole semitones instead of passing them through as a continuous voltage
Allow input to track multiple octaves — lets the root input move the chord across octaves rather than folding it into one
